mainTopic: Whether an item already טמא can take on more טומאה (שבע ליה טומאה), and how the halves of a divided עשרון join for טומאה and קמיצה.
overview: The amud has two topics, and both deal with טומאה. First the גמרא looks at רבא's question: can an item that is already טמא take on another טומאה, or is it already 'full' (שבע ליה טומאה)? אביי tries to prove from רבי יוסי's ruling about a מדרס sheet turned into a curtain that a second טומאה does take hold. רבא answers that the זב may have touched the sheet before lying on it, and a severe טומאה can always land on a light one. A second proof, from two folded sheets a זב sat on, is turned away because there both טומאות came at the same moment. So the question stays unresolved. Then רבא rules about an עשרון split in two, where one half was lost, replaced, and found again: which halves join together for טומאה, and which may be eaten after קמיצה. אביי disagrees and holds that all three halves belong to one group. רב פפא and רב יצחק בריה דרב משרשיא challenge אביי, and רב אשי defends him: the קומץ follows the כהן's intention for one full עשרון.

steps.title: A treading-impure sheet made into a curtain
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a sheet that was טמא מדרס and then made into a curtain loses its מדרס status but stays טמא with מגע מדרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a sheet had treading-impurity and someone made it into a curtain, it is pure from treading-impurity, but it is impure because of contact with a treading-impure item.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting the end of a משנה about a cloth that became טמא מדרס and was then made into a curtain. This sets up the source that אביי will use for his challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מדרס טומאה only applies to things made for sitting or lying on, so a curtain can no longer carry it. But the משנה says a lighter טומאה stays behind. It treats the cloth as if it 'touched' a מדרס, meaning itself before it changed.

keyTerms.meaning: Treading-impurity: severe טומאה that a זב gives to an item made for sitting or lying on, by pressing on it
A curtain, which is not used for sitting or lying
A lighter טומאה that comes from touching a מדרס item
Pure, not carrying טומאה

phrases.english: [A sheet that was impure with] treading-impurity, and he made it into a curtain:
it is pure from treading-impurity,
but it is impure with contact-of-treading impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quotation of the משנה that the challenge is built on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מדרס sheet made into a curtain is no longer טמא מדרס, but it is טמא מגע מדרס.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: the curtain is impure from the זב's touch
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי disagrees with 'מגע מדרס' and says the leftover טומאה is מגע הזב, in a case where the זב touched the sheet.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: Which treading-impure item did this curtain touch? Rather, if the זב touched it, it is impure with מגע הזב impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי asks how the curtain could be 'touching a מדרס', since nothing else touched it. He explains the rule differently: it stays impure only if the זב himself touched it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי rejects the idea that the cloth can count as touching itself. He switches the source of the leftover טומאה to the זב's direct touch, which a curtain can still carry. This is the line אביי will build his challenge on.

keyTerms.meaning: A man with a discharge who is a major source of טומאה
The טומאה an item gets from being touched by a זב
Rather, which introduces a corrected explanation

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:
Which treading-impure item did this touch?
Rather, if the zav touched it,
it is impure with contact-of-the-zav impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: בְּאֵיזֶה מִדְרָס נָגַע זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the explanation in step 1 and offers a different source for the remaining טומאה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The curtain stays impure only with מגע הזב, if the זב touched it directly.

steps.title: אביי: the zav's touch works even after treading-impurity
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that רבי יוסי's ruling seems to cover a case where the זב touched the sheet after it was already טמא מדרס. That means a second טומאה took hold, which contradicts רבא's suggestion of שבע ליה טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the zav touched it, in any case it is impure, even if this happened at the end: first it was impure with treading, and afterward came the zav's contact. Why? Let us say it is already full of impurity!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבא's suggestion that an item which is already טמא can't take on more טומאה. רבי יוסי's ruling seems to say that the זב's touch counts even when it came after the מדרס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the זב touched the sheet after it was already טמא מדרס, רבא's suggested rule would say the touch should do nothing, because the sheet is 'full'. Yet רבי יוסי says the curtain stays טמא מגע הזב. So a טומאה added later does take effect, which goes against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: It is 'full' of טומאה, so already impure that no further טומאה can take hold
In any case, at least
At the end, afterward
Why? A challenge word

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not questioning רבי יוסי. He is using רבי יוסי's ruling to attack רבא's principle of שבע ליה טומאה.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי נָגַע בּוֹ הַזָּב מִיהָא טָמֵא,
phrases.english: When the zav touched it, in any case it is impure,
phrases.notes: The one speaking here is אביי, challenging רבא.

phrases.english: and even if it was at the end,

phrases.aramaic: כְּטָמֵא מִדְרָס, וְאַחַר כָּךְ מַגַּע הַזָּב,
phrases.english: such as: first impure with treading, and afterward the zav's contact,
why? Let us say: it is already full of impurity!

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי נָגַע בּוֹ הַזָּב מִיהָא טָמֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי יוסי's ruling from step 2 to challenge רבא's principle.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's principle that an item already טמא cannot receive more טומאה (שבע ליה טומאה).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי's ruling seems to include a case where the זב touched the sheet after it was טמא מדרס, so a second, later טומאה did take hold.

steps.title: רבא: the touch may have come before the treading
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that רבי יוסי may mean the זב touched the sheet first. Then the severe מדרס טומאה landed on top of the lighter טומאה, and that is possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: From where do you know that this 'if the zav touched it' happened after the treading-impurity? Perhaps it happened before the treading-impurity, so it is a severe impurity coming on top of a light impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects אביי's reading of the order of events. He suggests the זב touched the sheet before lying on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's suggestion only blocks a lighter or equal טומאה from landing on an item that is already טמא. A heavier טומאה can still take hold on top of a lighter one. If the touch came first, the touch gave light טומאה and the מדרס then added severe טומאה. So רבי יוסי's case fits רבא's principle.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know? This questions an assumption
Perhaps, which offers another way to read the case
After / before
Severe טומאה, such as מדרס
Light טומאה, such as מגע הזב

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא's suggestion (which the גמרא leaves unresolved), an item that is already טמא cannot take on another light טומאה. But a severe טומאה can still take hold on top of a light one, so the order of events matters.

phrases.english: He said to him:
And from where [do you know] that this 'if the zav touched it'
is after the treading-impurity?
Perhaps it is before the treading-impurity,

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָוְיָא טוּמְאָה חֲמוּרָה עַל טוּמְאָה קַלָּה.
phrases.english: so that it is a severe impurity on top of a light impurity.
phrases.notes: The מדרס is the severe one, and the זב's touch is the light one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וּמִמַּאי דְּהַאי ״שֶׁאִם נָגַע בּוֹ הַזָּב״ לְבָתַר מִדְרָס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from step 3 by changing the assumed order of events.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: the touch came before the מדרס, not after.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי assumed the זב touched the sheet after it was already טמא מדרס.
steps.terutzMaskana: The touch may have come first. A severe טומאה can take hold on top of a light one, so רבא's rule stands.

steps.title: Two light impurities are different
steps.stepSummary: The proof from רבי יוסי only shows that a severe טומאה can land on a light one. In our case both טומאות are light, so the second may not take hold.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here, where both are light impurities, the second one does not take hold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes pushing away the proof from רבי יוסי. It says his case does not match the case we are asking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יוסי's case the second טומאה (מדרס) was more severe than the first, so it could still land. In the case under discussion both טומאות are light, so we can still say the item is already 'full' of טומאה. The question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one, meaning both of them
Here, meaning the case we are actually asking about

phrases.english: But here, where this one and that one
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the case we were really asking about, not רבי יוסי's sheet.

phrases.english: are both light impurity, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל הָכָא, דְּאִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי טוּמְאָה קַלָּה – לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes step 4's point: severe on light works, but that does not prove light on light.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from רבי יוסי's ruling of מגע הזב against שבע ליה טומאה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: His case is a severe טומאה on a light one, while the case in question is two light טומאות.

steps.title: A new proof from the two folded sheets
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries the סיפא: רבי יוסי agrees that when a זב sits on two stacked sheets, the bottom sheet gets both מדרס and מגע מדרס. Why isn't it 'full' of טומאה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, prove it from the last part: רבי יוסי agrees that if two folded sheets lie one on top of the other and a זב sat on them, the top one is טמא מדרס, and the bottom one is טמא מדרס and also מגע מדרס. But why? Let us say it is already full of טומאה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the first proof and brings a new one from a later part of the ברייתא. Here the bottom sheet seems to get two טומאות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The זב's weight presses on both sheets, so both become מדרס. The bottom sheet also touches the top sheet, which is מדרס, so it gets מגע מדרס too. If שבע ליה טומאה were true, the second טומאה should not take hold.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a source
Agrees, admits
Folded sheets
The top one / the bottom one

phrases.english: Rather, from the last clause:
Rabbi Yosei agrees
regarding two folded sheets
placed one on top of the other
and a zav sat on them,
that the top one is impure with midras,
and the bottom one is impure with midras
and with contact with midras.
But why? Let us say it is already full of impurity!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was turned away, a new proof is brought from the later clause.
steps.raayaObject: That an item does not become 'full' of טומאה, so a second טומאה can take hold.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the ברייתא: רבי יוסי agrees the bottom folded sheet is both מדרס and מגע מדרס.

steps.title: Same moment versus one after the other
steps.stepSummary: The proof fails: on the sheets both טומאות came at the same moment, while in our case they come one after the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it happened at the same time; here, it is one after the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns away the new proof by pointing out a difference in timing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the bottom sheet, מדרס and מגע מדרס landed in the same instant, so the sheet was never already 'full' first. שבע ליה טומאה only matters when one טומאה is already there before the second arrives, so the question stays unresolved.

keyTerms.meaning: There, meaning the case of the sheets
At the same moment
One after the other

steps.whatToRemember: Two proofs against שבע ליה טומאה were tried and both were turned away. Severe on light, or two at once, can work. Light on light, one after the other, is still an open question.

phrases.english: There, at the same time;
here, one after the other.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם בְּבַת אַחַת, הָכָא בְּזֶה אַחַר זֶה
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the two folded sheets.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There both טומאות arrive at once, while the question is about one arriving after the other.

steps.title: A divided tenth: which halves join for impurity
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules about an עשרון split in two, where one half was lost, replaced, and then found. If the lost half becomes טמא, it joins with the original other half, but not with the replacement.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: An עשרון was divided into two. One half was lost, and he set aside another half in its place. Then the lost one was found, and all three lie together in one vessel. If the lost one became טמא, the lost one and the first one join together and are both טמא, but the replacement does not join.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ruling from רבא about when pieces of a מנחה in one vessel join together for טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lost half and the original other half came from the same עשרון, so the vessel joins them and the טומאה spreads. The replacement half is not counted as joined to the lost half, so it stays טהור even though it sits in the same vessel.

keyTerms.meaning: A tenth of an איפה, the measure of a מנחה
The half that was lost
The half set aside as a replacement
A vessel or container
Join together and count as one for טומאה

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the word 'ראשון'. In 'ונמצא הראשון' it means the half that was lost and then found. In the rulings that follow ('אבוד וראשון מצטרפין'), it means the original other half that was never lost.

phrases.english: Rava said:
A tenth of an ephah that he divided,
and one of the halves was lost,
and he set aside another in its place,
and the first one was found,
phrases.notes: Here 'the first' means the half that had been lost, which now turns up again.

phrases.english: and all three are lying in one vessel:
if the lost one became impure,
the lost one and the first one join together,
phrases.notes: Now 'first' means the original other half that was never lost. A vessel joins its contents for טומאה of קדשים.

phrases.english: the replacement does not join.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, not connected to the שבע ליה טומאה discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the lost half becomes טמא, it joins with the original other half and both are טמא, but the replacement half does not join and stays טהור.

steps.title: When the replacement or the first half becomes impure
steps.stepSummary: רבא continues: if the replacement half becomes טמא, it joins only with the first half. If the first half becomes טמא, both other halves join with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the replacement half became impure, the replacement and the first half join together, but the lost half does not join. If the first half became impure, both of the others join with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא continues his ruling from the last step and covers the other two cases: the replacement becoming טמא, and the first half becoming טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The replacement was set aside to complete the first half, so the two are partners, and the lost-and-found half is left out. The first half was once partnered with the lost half and is now partnered with the replacement. So it links to both of them.

keyTerms.meaning: The half that was set aside as a replacement for the lost half
The half that was lost and later found
The first half, which was never lost
They join together, here meaning they share the טומאה as one unit

phrases.english: If the separated one became impure –
phrases.notes: "Separated" means the half set aside to replace the lost one.

phrases.english: the separated one and the first one join together,
the lost one does not join;
if the first one became impure –
both of them join together.
phrases.notes: "Both" means the lost half and the replacement both join with the first half.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's three-case ruling begun in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Replacement טמא: it joins with the first half only. First half טמא: both other halves join.

steps.title: אביי: all the pieces always join
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that whichever piece becomes טמא, the other two join with it, because all three belong to the same מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי says: even if any one of them became impure, both of the others join together with it. Why? They are all members of one household.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי disagrees with רבא and says there is no difference between the cases. Any piece that becomes טמא passes it on to both others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא linked only the halves meant to complete each other. אביי looks at the bigger picture: all three pieces were set aside for one single מנחה. So they all count as one family for טומאה, even the lost half and the replacement.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'residents of one cabin': they all belong together as one group
Even if any one of them became impure

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not only talking about the first half. He says that even when the lost half or the replacement becomes טמא, all three join. This is exactly where he disagrees with רבא.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
even if any one of them became impure as well –
both of them join together,
phrases.notes: Here "both" means the other two pieces, whichever ones they are.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
They are all residents of one cabin with each other.
phrases.notes: A picture-phrase: they all belong to the same one מנחה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ נִטְמָא אֶחָד מֵהֶן נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing view to רבא's ruling in steps 8–9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any one piece becoming טמא makes the other two join, since all three belong to one מנחה.

steps.title: The same rule for taking the handful: from the lost or the replacement half
steps.stepSummary: רבא applies his logic to קמיצה. Taking the handful from the lost half permits it and the first half, but not the replacement. Taking it from the replacement permits it and the first half, but not the lost half.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the same applies to taking the handful. If he took the handful from the lost half, its leftovers and the first half are eaten, but the replacement is not eaten. If he took the handful from the replacement, its leftovers and the first half are eaten, but the lost half is not eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now uses רבא's same pairing idea for קמיצה, the taking of a handful that permits the rest of a מנחה to be eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A handful permits only the one עשרון it was taken for. Whichever of the two other halves the handful came from becomes paired with the first half, and those two are eaten. The third piece is left out and may not be eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking a handful of flour from a מנחה to burn on the מזבח
He took the handful
The leftovers of the מנחה after the handful is taken, eaten by the כהנים
They are eaten, meaning they are permitted to the כהנים

phrases.english: And similarly regarding taking the handful,
phrases.notes: This continues רבא's approach, not אביי's.

phrases.english: if he took the handful from the lost one –
its remainder and the first one are eaten,
the separated one is not eaten;
if he took the handful from the separated one –
its remainder and the first one are eaten,
the lost one is not eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from אביי's view to apply רבא's pairing logic to קמיצה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A handful taken from the lost half or the replacement permits that half with the first half. The third piece stays forbidden.

steps.title: Taking the handful from the first half
steps.stepSummary: If the handful is taken from the first half, neither the lost half nor the replacement may be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he took the handful from the first half, both of them are not eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the קמיצה cases with the hardest one: the handful is taken from the first half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half is linked to both the lost half and the replacement, but a handful can only permit one עשרון. We cannot tell which of the two it permitted. So neither one may be eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: Neither of the two may be eaten

steps.whatToRemember: For רבא, pieces join only when they truly complete one עשרון together. The first half pairs with both of the others, so for טומאה both join with it. For קמיצה, neither of them is permitted, since we cannot know which one the handful worked for. אביי holds that all three pieces belong to one group.
steps.whyThisMatters: The same pairing idea gives opposite-looking results. For טומאה, being linked to two pieces makes both of them join, while for eating it makes both of them forbidden.

phrases.english: if he took the handful from the first one –
both of them are not eaten.
phrases.notes: Both the lost half and the replacement are forbidden, because the handful can only permit one of them and we don't know which.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the קמיצה cases from step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A handful taken from the first half leaves both the lost half and the replacement forbidden to eat.

steps.title: אביי: whichever half the handful is taken from, the other two may not be eaten
steps.stepSummary: אביי disagrees with רבא about the קומץ. If it is taken from any one of the three halves, both of the other halves are forbidden to eat, because all three pieces are tied together.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Even if the כהן took the handful from any one of them, the other two are not eaten. Why? Because all of them are 'residents of one cabin' with each other.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives his own ruling on the קומץ case, arguing against רבא's ruling from Steps 11-12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said it matters which half the קומץ came from. אביי says it does not matter. Just as he ruled about טומאה in Step 10, all three halves count as one connected group. So we cannot say the קומץ permitted one specific other half, and both other halves stay forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ קָמַץ מֵאֶחָד מֵהֶן,
phrases.english: Abaye said: Even if he took the handful from one of them,
phrases.notes: "One of them" means any of the three halves: the lost one, the replacement, or the first half.

phrases.english: both of them are not eaten.
phrases.notes: "Both" means the two halves the handful was not taken from.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלְּהוּ נָמֵי בְּנֵי בִיקְתָּא דַּהֲדָדֵי נִינְהוּ.
phrases.english: All of them are residents of one cabin with each other.

steps.triggerLanguage: אביי אמר: אפילו קמץ מאחד מהן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: אביי disputes רבא's קמיצה rulings, using the same reasoning he gave about טומאה in Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the קומץ is taken from any one of the three halves, the other two halves may not be eaten, since all three are part of one מנחה.

steps.title: רב פפא: then even the half the handful came from should not be eaten
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges אביי. If the קומץ counts for all three halves, then part of it went toward an extra half. That means the half it was taken from did not get its full share of the קומץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא challenged it: And are its own leftovers at least eaten? But there is a sixth of the handful that was not offered for it!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא attacks אביי's ruling. He shows that it leads to a problem even with the half the קומץ was taken from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי treats all three halves (one and a half עשרון) as one group. So the קומץ was taken for all three, and one third of it was really 'for' the extra half. That means the real עשרון got less than a full קומץ. Each of its two halves is missing a sixth, so even the half the קומץ came from should not be permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged it; a sharp objection to a ruling
The leftovers of the מנחה after the קומץ is removed, which the כהנים eat
A sixth (literally a small coin worth one sixth)
Offered on the מזבח

phrases.english: Rav Pappa challenged it:
And are its own leftovers at least eaten?
phrases.notes: "Its own" means the half the handful was taken from. אביי seemed to allow that one.

phrases.aramaic: הָא אִיכָּא דַּנְקָא דְּקוֹמֶץ דְּלָא קָרֵיב!
phrases.english: But there is a sixth of the handful that was not offered!

steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's view that all three halves are one group for the קומץ
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the קומץ covers three halves, a third of it went to the extra half. So the real halves each lack a sixth of their קומץ, and even the half it was taken from should not be eaten.

steps.title: רב יצחק בריה דרב משרשיא: how can the handful itself be offered?
steps.stepSummary: A second challenge to אביי. If a third of the קומץ belongs to the extra half, which is not really part of the קרבן, then that third is ordinary חולין. So the קומץ itself should not be allowed on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק the son of רב משרשיא challenged it: And the handful itself, how can it be offered? There is a third that is non-sacred!
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא attacks אביי. This time the problem is not the leftovers but the קומץ itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra half was replaced, so it is not needed for the מנחה. If the קומץ was taken for all three halves, one third of it stands for that unneeded half. That third would be like חולין, and you cannot offer חולין on the מזבח together with the קומץ.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary, non-sacred food that may not be offered on the מזבח
A third
Itself

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא:
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak the son of Rav Mesharshiya challenged it:
And the handful itself, how can it be offered?
But there is a third that is non-sacred.
phrases.notes: This is the third of the handful that stands for the extra half, which isn't needed for the מנחה.

steps.triggerLanguage: מתקיף לה רב יצחק בריה דרב משרשיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, stronger challenge to אביי that builds on the same math as Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's view that the קומץ counts for all three halves
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A third of the קומץ would stand for the unneeded extra half and be חולין, so the קומץ could not be offered at all.

steps.title: רב אשי: the handful follows the כהן's intention, and he means a full עשרון
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי defends אביי. The קומץ depends on what the כהן has in mind, and he always intends it for one full עשרון. So none of the קומץ is 'for' the extra half. Both challenges fall away, while the uncertainty about which other half was permitted remains.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: With the handful, the matter depends on the intention of the כהן. And when the כהן takes the handful, he takes it for a tenth.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers both challenges and keeps אביי's ruling standing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenges assumed the קומץ is split evenly among all three halves. רב אשי says no: the כהן intends the קומץ for exactly one עשרון. So the whole קומץ counts for the real מנחה, and nothing in it is חולין or missing. But we still don't know which of the other two halves joins the half it was taken from to make that עשרון, so both stay forbidden, as אביי said.

keyTerms.meaning: The intention of the כהן
The matter depends (on)
A tenth of an איפה, the full measure of this מנחה

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, all three halves are one group, so the other two can't be eaten. רב אשי explains that this does not ruin the קומץ, because the כהן intends it for exactly one עשרון.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
With the handful, the matter depends on the intention of the priest,
and when the priest takes the handful,
he takes it for a tenth.
phrases.notes: He means one full עשרון, not the extra half.

steps.triggerLanguage: רב אשי אמר: קומץ בדעתא דכהן תליא מילתא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenges of Steps 14 and 15 and defends אביי's ruling from Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the assumption: the קומץ is not divided among all three halves but follows the כהן's intent for one עשרון.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קומץ was taken equally for all three halves, so part of it is wasted on the extra half or is חולין.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כהן intends the קומץ for exactly one עשרון. So the whole קומץ is valid and fully counts, but the other two halves still can't be eaten, since we don't know which one completes the עשרון.
